```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(SigBridgeR)
library(Seurat)
```

# Overview

`BenchAcc()` compute the classification accuracy of screening methods according to a known ground truth

It treats `"Positive"` as the positive class and every other supported label
(`"Negative"`, `"Neutral"`, `"Other"`) as the negative class. For each screening
method found in the object, it computes a full set of binary classification
metrics, so the methods can be ranked or compared on exactly the same cells.

The function accepts three kinds of input:

* a `Seurat` object whose `meta.data` contains one column per screening method;
* a `ScreenMethodResult`, which is unwrapped to its `scRNA_data` slot;
* a `BenchAccConfig`, which runs every configured screening method first and
  then evaluates the merged labels in one pass.

# A small example

The example below uses a tiny object with six cells, a ground-truth column and
two simulated screening results. In a real analysis the `Scissor` and `scPAS`
columns would be produced by `Screen()` or `MergeResult()`.

```{r}
#| label: benchacc-basic
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
  matrix(
    seq_len(24L),
    nrow = 4L,
    dimnames = list(paste0("Gene", 1:4), paste0("Cell", 1:6))
  ),
  sparse = TRUE
)

sc <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)

sc$truth <- c(
  "Positive",
  "Negative",
  "Positive",
  "Other",
  "Positive",
  "Negative"
)
sc$Scissor <- c(
  "Positive",
  "Negative",
  "Positive",
  "Other",
  "Negative",
  "Negative"
)
sc$scPAS <- c(
  "Positive",
  "Positive",
  "Negative",
  "Other",
  "Negative",
  "Negative"
)

metrics <- BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE)

round(do.call(rbind, metrics), 3)
```

Each element of the returned list is a one-row matrix whose row name is the
screening method. The same numbers are easier to compare after binding them:

```{r}
#| label: benchacc-bind
metrics_dt <- data.table::rbindlist(
  lapply(metrics, as.data.frame),
  idcol = "method"
)

metrics_dt[, .(method, TPR, FPR, F1, Accuracy, Precision, Recall)]
```

# Specifying the ground truth

`bench_config` can be given in two equivalent forms:

```{r}
#| label: benchacc-truth-forms
# * a length-one column name in sc@meta.data
from_column <- BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE)

# * a per-cell label vector, one label per cell
from_vector <- BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = sc$truth, verbose = FALSE)

identical(from_column, from_vector)
```

The labels must contain `"Positive"`, and the vector form must have one element
per cell. The function stops with an informative error when the column is
missing, when the labels have no positive class, or when the vector length does
not match the number of cells:

```{r}
#| label: benchacc-validation
#| error: true
BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "missing_column", verbose = FALSE)
```

# Reading the metrics

With \(P\) positive and \(N\) negative ground-truth cells, and \(TP\), \(FP\),
\(TN\), \(FN\) the usual confusion-matrix counts, `BenchAcc()` reports:

| Metric | Definition | Meaning |
|--------|------------|---------|
| `TPR` / `Recall` | \(TP / (TP + FN)\) | Fraction of truly positive cells recovered |
| `FPR` | \(FP / (FP + TN)\) | Fraction of negative cells incorrectly called positive |
| `TNR` | \(TN / (TN + FP)\) | Fraction of negative cells correctly left out |
| `FNR` | \(FN / (FN + TP)\) | Fraction of positive cells missed |
| `Precision` | \(TP / (TP + FP)\) | Fraction of called cells that are truly positive |
| `F1` | \(2TP / (2TP + FP + FN)\) | Harmonic mean of precision and recall |
| `Accuracy` | \((TP + TN) / (P + N)\) | Overall agreement with the ground truth |

Because screening methods usually return only a small positive set, `Accuracy`
tends to be high and similar across methods. `TPR`/`Recall`, `Precision` and
`F1` are usually more informative when comparing methods. A method that selects
very few cells can have perfect precision but low recall, while a permissive
method can have high recall but many false positives.

`BenchAcc()` only scores screening method columns. Other metadata columns,
including the ground-truth column itself, are ignored. Method names are matched
case-insensitively against the methods registered in `ScreenStrategy`:

```{r}
#| label: benchacc-case
sc$SCISSOR <- sc$Scissor
sc$Scissor <- NULL

names(BenchAcc(sc, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE))
```

# Benchmarking the screening step

If the screening has not been run yet, wrap the inputs in a `BenchAccConfig`.
The configuration stores the bulk data, the single-cell object, the phenotype
and the methods to run. `BenchAcc()` then screens the data with each method and
evaluates the accumulated labels:

```{r}
#| label: benchacc-config
#| eval: false
config <- BenchAccConfig(
  matched_bulk = bulk,
  sc_data = sc,
  phenotype = phenotype,
  label_type = "{method_name}",
  phenotype_class = "binary",
  screen_method = c("Scissor", "scPAS"),
  method_param = MethodParamSet(
    Scissor_param = list(alpha = 0.05),
    scPAS_param = list(alpha = 0.01)
  ),
  bench_config = "truth"
)

acc <- BenchAcc(config, verbose = FALSE)
```

The `bench_config` of a `BenchAccConfig` is validated when the object is
created, so an invalid ground truth fails early instead of after a long
screening run. `method_param` is the place for method-specific arguments; see
`?MethodParamSet` for the full list of fields.

# Practical notes

* **Use the same cells for every method.** `BenchAcc()` compares the labels
  cell by cell. Merge the screening results first (for example with
  `MergeResult()`) so that every method shares the same cell names and order.
* **Use an independent ground truth.** A label derived from the same bulk
  phenotype that drove the screening is not an independent validation; use
  marker-based annotation, an external cell-type reference or held-out
  experimental labels when possible.
* **Report more than accuracy.** `TPR`, `Precision` and `F1` describe the
  trade-off between missing positive cells and including negative ones, which
  is usually the relevant question for phenotype-associated cell screening.
* **Only the four supported labels are accepted.** Predicted labels must be
  one of `"Positive"`, `"Negative"`, `"Neutral"` or `"Other"`; typos and `NA`
  abort with the offending column and row.

# See also

* `BenchGSEA()` for comparing the functional signal of the selected cells.
* `BenchGeneScore()` for comparing pathway activity at the single-cell level.
* `BenchMemory()` for comparing run time and memory.
* `BenchAccConfig()`, `MethodParamSet()` and `?Screen` for the configuration
  and screening interfaces.
